chapterNote: The Old Hundredth — five verses that have carried more congregational praise than perhaps any other lines ever written, the psalm behind 'All People That on Earth Do Dwell' and the common doxology. It is a liturgy of approach in seven commands: shout, serve, come, know, enter, thank, bless. The invitation is scandalous in its width — all the earth, every land, summoned through Israel's gates — and the theology is compact as a coin. Know that the LORD, He is God: He made us, and we are His; His people, the sheep of His pasture. The gates are entered with thanksgiving because of who stands at the center: the LORD is good, His covenant love is forever, and His faithfulness runs to generation after generation. Three measures of God — goodness for the present, chesed for every circumstance, faithfulness for all time to come — and therefore joy is not the mood of the lucky but the duty and privilege of everyone He made.

1.text: A psalm for the thank offering. Raise the joyful shout to the LORD, all the earth!
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of praise ['thanksgiving', todah, the KJV margin]. Make a joyful noise [rua — raise the shout] unto the LORD [YHWH], all ye lands ['all the earth', kol ha-eretz, the KJV margin].
1.notes: todah (H8426) is the thank offering itself: a psalm written to accompany sacrifice, gratitude with a liturgy. rua (H7321) is the war-shout and coronation-shout repurposed for joy — and the summons goes past Israel to kol ha-eretz (H776), the whole earth, every land invited to Zion's gate.

2.text: Serve the LORD with gladness; come into His presence with a ringing song.
2.amp: Serve [avad] the LORD [YHWH] with gladness [simchah]: come [bo] before His presence [panim] with singing [renanah — ringing, jubilant song].
2.notes: avad (H5647) is the one word for serving and worshiping — the psalm insists the two are one act, and stipulates the manner: simchah (H8057), gladness. Sour service is a contradiction in terms here; the road into His panim (H6440) is paved with renanah.

3.text: Know this: the LORD, He is God. It is He who made us, and we are His — His people, and the sheep of His pasture.
3.amp: Know [yada] ye that the LORD [YHWH] He is God [Elohim]: it is He that has made [asah] us, and not we ourselves ['and His we are', the KJV margin]; we are His people [am], and the sheep [tson] of His pasture [marith].
3.notes: The creed at the psalm's center: yada (H3045), know — praise must run on knowledge. The Hebrew margin preserves the richer reading: He made us, 'and His we are' — creation grounding ownership. am and tson (H5971, H6629): a people for belonging, sheep for dependence, His marith for provision (cf. Psalm 95:7; John 10:14).

4.text: Enter His gates with thanksgiving, His courts with praise; give thanks to Him, and bless His name.
4.amp: Enter [bo] into His gates [shaar] with thanksgiving [todah], and into His courts [chatser] with praise [tehillah]: be thankful [yadah] unto Him, and bless [barak] His name [shem].
4.notes: The procession moves inward: shaar to chatser (H8179, H2691), gates to courts, with todah and tehillah (H8426, H8416) as the admission carried in the hands. yadah (H3034) and barak (H1288): thanksgiving for what He gives, blessing for who He is — the shem (H8034) praised above the gifts.

5.text: For the LORD is good; His covenant love endures forever, and His faithfulness stands to generation after generation.
5.amp: For the LORD [YHWH] is good [tov]; His mercy [chesed — covenant love] is everlasting [olam]; and His truth [emunah — faithfulness] endures to all generations ['to generation and generation', dor, the KJV margin].
5.notes: The 'for' that carries all seven commands: tov (H2896) in His character, chesed (H2617) le-olam in His covenant, emunah (H530) dor va-dor in His keeping. This closing formula became Israel's most-repeated refrain (cf. Psalm 136; 2 Chronicles 5:13) — three tenses of confidence: good now, loving forever, faithful to every generation still coming.
